h1: The 8 Best Narrow Nightstands of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 narrow nightstands compared on width, charging, storage and capacity, from 7-inch shelves to a farmhouse drawer table.
summary: The LOAKEKEL narrow nightstand is the best overall: 7.87 inches wide with two AC outlets, USB-A, USB-C and two fabric drawers. The matching set doubles it for couples. The Giantex carries the most weight at 210 lb, the Vantimo is the narrowest, and HOOBRO, Furinno, Yoobure and Homleke cover quick assembly, certified materials, a basket and reading nooks.
intro: Nobody buys a narrow nightstand because they want one. They buy it because the gap between the bed and the wall is nine inches, or the door swings into any wider table. That makes this category a numbers game from the start: measure the gap, subtract an inch for clearance, and only then ask what a slim table can hold, because every inch of width removed takes storage with it.

Eight narrow tables are ranked here, spanning open shelves, closed drawers and charging models. Where a source listed width and depth in a confusing order, we treated the smallest dimension as the narrow side. The order starts with how much storage and power each manages to extract from its footprint, then looks at capacity, stability and how the table sits next to a bed.

products.name: LOAKEKEL Narrow Nightstand with USB-C
products.verdict: 7.87 inches wide with a full charging station and two closed fabric drawers.
products.description:
The LOAKEKEL is the narrow nightstand that does the most with the least width. At 15.75 by 7.87 by 23.22 inches in engineered wood and metal, it carries two AC outlets, a USB-A port, a USB-C port, an LED light and two fabric drawers rated for 44 lb. Charging at the bedside is the feature a slim open shelf cannot offer.

It wins because it is among the narrowest tables with charging that still gives closed drawers. The open-shelf models are slimmer but give you neither power nor hidden storage, and it sits in the $25 to $50 bucket.

Buy it for a tight bedroom that needs power at hand. The caveat is the fabric drawers: they suit light items such as chargers and eye masks, not heavy objects, and they cost more than a plain shelf.
products.skipIf: You want a plain open shelf.

products.name: LOAKEKEL Narrow Nightstand Set of 2
products.verdict: Two matching charging nightstands with a lifetime warranty.
products.description:
The set of two LOAKEKEL tables makes the pairing easy. Each table measures 15.74 by 7.87 by 23.22 inches, with two AC outlets, a USB-A port, a USB-C port and two fabric drawers, and the listing includes a lifetime warranty. Symmetry matters in a bedroom, and matching hardware means both sides look alike.

It ranks second because a pair suits couples sharing a narrow room, and buying two at once avoids hunting for a compatible second table later. It is the single-table LOAKEKEL times two, in the $25 to $50 bucket.

Best for a shared bedroom where both sleepers want to charge a phone. The caveat is obvious: it only makes sense if you want two, so a single sleeper should take the single table and save the space and the money.

products.name: Giantex Farmhouse Narrow Nightstand
products.verdict: A 210 lb capacity with a pull-out drawer, two shelves and rubberwood legs.
products.description:
The Giantex is the strongest here. It measures 23.5 by 12 by 24.5 inches in engineered wood and MDF with rubberwood legs, with one pull-out drawer, two shelves and non-slip pads, and has the highest stated capacity at 210 lb. That means a lamp, books and a water carafe will not strain it.

It ranks third because it is the sturdiest but not very narrow at 12 inches, which rules it out of the tightest gaps. It beats the shelf models on storage, and sits in the $50 to $100 bucket.

Buy it for a bedside that carries a lot. The caveat is the larger footprint and the lack of charging, so a nightstand that must slide into a nine inch gap should be one of the slimmer tables, and you will run an extension cord for your phone.

products.name: Vantimo 3-Tier Narrow Nightstand
products.verdict: Only 7.08 inches wide, with three open tiers and adjustable footpads.
products.description:
The Vantimo is the narrowest table in the group. It measures 7.08 by 16.92 by 22.24 inches in particleboard with a black metal frame, with three open tiers, a 40 lb capacity, adjustable footpads and a stain-resistant lacquered finish. It costs under $25, the cheapest pick.

It ranks fourth because it is the narrowest and cheapest, but it has no drawers or power. Open tiers show everything on them, so clutter reads as decor. It suits the tightest gaps better than anything else here.

Buy it for a very tight spot beside a bed or a door. The caveat is exposed storage, so keep the tiers tidy, and expect to run a cord for charging. Adjustable footpads help it sit steady on a slightly uneven floor.

products.name: HOOBRO Industrial Narrow Nightstand
products.verdict: Five-minute tool-free assembly and a 50 lb capacity.
products.description:
The HOOBRO is the quickest to put together. It measures 15 by 11 by 19.7 inches in engineered wood with a metal frame and two open shelves, and the listing states tool-free assembly in five minutes. It handles 50 lb, strong for its under $25 price, and has an industrial look.

It ranks fifth because it is fast to build and sturdy for the money, but it is the shortest here at 19.7 inches. That height suits a low bed only; with a standard mattress, you would be reaching down to the shelf.

Best for renters who want a fast setup and a table that moves easily. The caveat is the low height, so check your mattress top against the shelf, and remember open shelves leave cords and clutter visible beside the bed.
products.idealFor: Renters who want a quick build.

products.name: Furinno JUST 3-Tier Nightstand
products.verdict: FSC-certified and CARB-compliant with rounded corners.
products.description:
The Furinno is the one with credentials. It measures 13.4 by 11.5 by 22.8 inches in CARB-compliant composite wood with PVC tubes, with three open tiers and rounded corners. It is FSC certified, and costs under $25. Rounded corners are a small thing that matters in a small bedroom where you brush past a table at night.

It ranks sixth because the material credentials are good but 30 lb is the lowest capacity here. A heavy lamp and a stack of books will push it.

Best for a safety-minded buyer or a household with young children. The caveat is the low capacity and open shelves, so keep heavy items off it. If you need more strength, the Giantex at 210 lb is in another league.
products.skipIf: You need to hold heavier items.

products.name: Yoobure Narrow 3-Tier Nightstand with Basket
products.verdict: A narrow three-tier with a fitted storage basket.
products.description:
The Yoobure matches the LOAKEKEL's width without the power. It measures 7.9 by 16.5 by 24.5 inches in engineered wood and metal, with three tiers, one storage basket and adjustable footpads. The basket gives you the only closed storage among the open-tier tables, and 24.5 inches is the tallest of the no-charging narrow models.

It ranks seventh because the basket hides small items but nothing here charges a phone. It costs $25 to $50, the same as the LOAKEKEL.

Best for hiding small items on a narrow table, such as remotes and lotion. The caveat is no charging: if you want power at the bedside, the LOAKEKEL costs the same band and adds outlets and drawers, which makes it the better buy for most.
pros: Tallest of the no-charging narrow picks
cons: Basket is the only closed storage
products.idealFor: Narrow spaces that need some hidden storage.

products.name: Homleke Skinny Narrow Nightstand
products.verdict: A 7.1 inch deep shelf table with a removable mesh magazine basket.
products.description:
The Homleke is the thinnest shelf-style table here. It measures 7.1 by 16.9 by 23.6 inches in engineered wood and alloy steel, with a rust-resistant frame, adjustable feet and a removable iron mesh magazine basket. Seven inches deep is slim enough to tuck beside a sofa or a bed in a hallway.

It ranks last because it offers little beyond the Vantimo and Yoobure, though the basket is a unique touch for books and magazines. At $25 to $50 it costs more than the Vantimo.

Best for a reading nook where books are the main load. The caveat is no charging or drawers, and the dimensions are listed in an order that can confuse, so measure the footprint against your gap before ordering.

whatMatters.detail: Measure the space between the bed and the wall, then subtract an inch for clearance. A 7 inch table fits where a 12 inch table will not. Check every dimension in the listing, because width and depth are sometimes listed in confusing order, and mark the floor with painter's tape to test the footprint before you order, since a few inches decide the fit.

Tables near 7 inches wide hold less, and drawers and charging fit in only the more expensive ones. Decide whether you need hidden storage or just a surface. A narrow open shelf is cheaper and tidier if you keep little on it, but a closed drawer hides clutter at night, and only the LOAKEKEL tables add both drawers and power.

Stated capacities here run from 30 lb to 210 lb. A lamp, clock, books and a glass of water add up faster than you expect. Check the capacity in the listing and treat the lowest figures as suitable for light items only, not for heavy lamps or stacks of hardbacks, and never assume weight is spread evenly.

A 19.7 inch table sits below most mattresses, while heights near 23 to 25 inches suit standard beds. Compare the table height with your mattress top, since a nightstand that is too low means reaching down, and one that is too tall can crowd the pillow or lamp.

Narrow tables tip more easily than wide ones, particularly when drawers are open or a heavy lamp sits on top. Adjustable feet and non-slip pads help on uneven floors. Check the listing for them, and keep the heaviest items low and centered so the table does not lean when you reach for it in the dark.

faq.q: How narrow can a nightstand be?
faq.a: In this guide, the Vantimo is 7.08 inches wide and the Homleke is 7.1 inches deep, with the LOAKEKEL at 7.87. Measure your gap and subtract an inch for clearance, because a table that touches the wall is hard to open.

They can. Adjustable feet, as on the Vantimo and Yoobure, and non-slip pads on the Giantex help. Keep heavy items on the lowest tier and avoid overloading the top, and level the feet if the floor slopes.

faq.q: Can I get a narrow nightstand with charging?
faq.a: Yes. The LOAKEKEL has two AC outlets, USB-A and USB-C, and is available as a single or a set of two. None of the open-shelf models here charge a phone, so you would run a cord or a power strip.

faq.q: What is the strongest narrow nightstand?
faq.a: The Giantex is rated to 210 lb, though it is wider than the slimmest options at 12 inches. For a narrower gap, the HOOBRO handles 50 lb, and the Vantimo handles 40 lb at only 7.08 inches wide.
It indicates responsibly sourced wood. The Furinno lists FSC and CARB compliance, which suits households that care about materials and indoor air quality, though its capacity is only 30 lb.
The HOOBRO lists tool-free assembly in about five minutes. Others may take longer, so plan time to put together any drawer model such as the LOAKEKEL, and keep the screws until it is done.

finalTake: Buy the LOAKEKEL for a tight bedroom that needs power, or the set of two for both sides of the bed. Choose the Giantex if the table carries a lot, and the Vantimo when the gap is under eight inches. HOOBRO, Furinno, Yoobure and Homleke are narrower fits for specific habits.
